_note: Ranking Languages by How Many Sounds They Have. Count = median total of consonants + vowels + tones across all PHOIBLE 2.0 inventories for the language (marginal sounds excluded; sounds_data/count.py, sounds_data/ranking.json). Languages whose studies disagree a lot (Japanese 18-40, Spanish 25-45, Finnish 19-42, Hawaiian 13-19, Hungarian 39-65, Hindi 51-94) are left out. Circassian: Kabardian median 55 (Adyghe 59 in one study). Abkhaz dropped (no speech recording); Rotokas (11) has no recording, Pirahã (11, two studies agree) used instead.
title: Ranking Languages by How Many Sounds They Have
subtitle: CONSONANTS + VOWELS + TONES (SOURCE: PHOIBLE)
outro: Which sound is the hardest for you?

items.name: !Xóõ (Taa)
items.lit: clicks, the bulk of its 130 consonants
cards: 161 sounds in the study PHOIBLE lists: 130 consonants, most of them clicks, plus vowels and tones.
Only a few thousand people speak it, in Botswana and Namibia.

items.name: Xhosa
cards: 84 sounds in PHOIBLE's study, including about 15 to 20 clicks written with c, q and x.
Xhosa was Nelson Mandela's mother tongue.

items.name: Circassian
items.lit: Adyghe may have only about three
cards: Kabardian has about 55 sounds (studies say 51 to 63) and Adyghe about 59, almost all of them consonants.
A cousin, Ubykh, had over 80 consonants. It died with its last speaker in 1992.

items.name: English
cards: About 40 sounds (studies say 38 to 45, by dialect) but only 26 letters, which is why English spelling is so messy.
Its two th sounds, in 'think' and 'this', are rare among the world's languages.

items.name: German
cards: About 40 sounds (studies say 39 to 40), including ü and ö.
Two different ch sounds: soft in 'ich', throaty in 'Bach'.

items.name: Russian
cards: About 38 sounds (studies say 37 to 42).
Most consonants come in hard and soft pairs: 'мат' (checkmate) and 'мять' (to crumple).

items.name: Polish
cards: About 36 sounds (studies say 35 to 37).
sz and ś sound alike to English ears, but to Poles they are two different sounds.

items.name: Swahili
cards: About 35 sounds (studies say 33 to 36) and just five vowels.
Words can start with the ng of 'sing': 'ng'ombe' means cow.

items.name: Georgian
cards: 33 sounds in most studies: 28 consonants and only 5 vowels.
With so few vowels, consonants pile up: 'gvprtskvni' means 'you peel us'.

items.name: Yoruba
cards: About 31 sounds (studies say 27 to 32), plus three tones on top.
gb and kp are made with the lips and the back of the mouth at the same time.

items.name: Hebrew
items.lit: most people say them the same
cards: About 27 sounds (studies say 25 to 30) and only 5 vowels.
Most Israelis no longer pronounce the old throat sounds of ע and ח differently from א and כ.

items.name: Indonesian
cards: About 27 sounds (studies say 26 to 27).
Spelling matches sound almost perfectly, which makes it easy to read aloud.

items.name: Pirahã
items.lit: a real Pirahã word (with a rare lip trill)
cards: Only 11 sounds: 8 consonants and 3 vowels, both studies agree. One of the smallest sound systems known.
Pirahã can also be whistled and hummed, and it has no words for exact numbers.
